Sell the emotional fantasy of doing the hobby rather than merely depicting an object. Aim for the feel of a miniature lifestyle hero illustration inside one coherent collectible-art universe, not a poster, advertisement, editorial cover, card face, or designed page. Keep edges and subject readability cleaner than soft editorial painting. No text, no logo, no typography, no card border, no rarity badge, no watermark, no UI.

The hobby or interest name is semantic context only and must never appear visually. Never render the hobby name, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, body copy, text box, lower-third, or typography-like decoration. Do not reserve blank layout space for text and do not turn the composition into a poster, advertisement, magazine cover, card face, or editorial page. Use this overall composition approach: Show a real shared office environment first: several adult professionals independently working side by side at communal desks, with distinct personal work setups and one small natural interaction. The spatial cue of shared desks, varied seating, laptops/notebooks, mugs, headphones, plants, and shared amenities must carry the concept. Do not use a craft bench, laboratory, makerspace, assembly table, hand tools, microscopes, jewelry, machine parts, or apprentice scene. Human-height medium-wide office view that makes the communal desk layout and multiple independent workers unmistakable. The emotional feeling should be independence, belonging, focus, productive energy.
